name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
summary: UNESCO World Heritage Baroque basilica consecrated in 1605 holding the sacred relic of St. Francis Xavier.
description: The Basilica of Bom Jesus in Old Goa is one of the most revered Christian pilgrimage shrines in Asia and a masterpiece of Portuguese Baroque architecture. Constructed of exposed red laterite stone with an ornate carved basaltic facade, it houses the silver casket and mortal remains of Saint Francis Xavier.
history: Consecrated in May 1605 by Archbishop Dom Fr. Aleixo de Menezes. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
culture: Hosts the feast of St. Francis Xavier drawing thousands of international pilgrims; features gilded baroque altars and Flemish woodcarvings.

name: Se Cathedral
summary: One of the largest churches in Asia, consecrated in 1619, known for its Portuguese-Manueline architecture and Golden Bell.
description: Se Cathedral (Sé Catedral de Santa Catarina) is the seat of the Patriarch of the East Indies. Built to commemorate Portuguese victory over an invading Muslim army on the Feast of Saint Catherine, it boasts a Tuscan exterior, gilded Corinthian altars, and the resonant Golden Bell (Sino de Ouro).
history: Commissioned by Afonso de Albuquerque; commenced in 1562 under King Dom Sebastião and completed in 1619. Inscribed under UNESCO World Heritage in 1986.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Fort Aguada
summary: 17th-century Portuguese fortress and 4-storey lighthouse standing proudly on Sinquerim Beach overlooking the Arabian Sea.
description: Constructed in 1612 to protect Portuguese maritime trade routes against Dutch fleets and the Marathas, Fort Aguada features formidable laterite stone ramparts and an enormous freshwater cistern that supplied fresh water to merchant ships.
history: Built in 1612 during Portuguese rule under King Philip II. It mounted 79 cannons and possessed one of Asia earliest 19th-century light towers.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Dudhsagar Falls
summary: Four-tiered Sea of Milk waterfall plummeting 310 meters on the Mandovi River along the Western Ghats within Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary.
description: Dudhsagar is one of India tallest and most majestic waterfalls, cascading through lush Western Ghats tropical rainforests. Famous for the railway bridge spanning directly across the waterfall spray.
history: Ancient Konkan landmark surrounded by tribal legend of the virtuous princess who poured milk to shield her privacy.
best_time_to_visit: October to May for safe jeep access; monsoon for dramatic roaring flow
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Mollem National Park
summary: Core area of Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary in the Western Ghats holding evergreen rainforests, leopards, and 12th-century Tambdi Surla temple.
description: Mollem National Park protects biodiversity-rich Western Ghats tropical rainforests home to Bengal tigers, black panthers, barking deer, and hornbills. Houses the 12th-century Kadamba-era basalt temple of Mahadeva at Tambdi Surla.
history: Notified as a national park in 1978; contains ancient Kadamba dynasty temple architecture.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Calangute Beach
summary: Goa largest and most famous beach strip, renowned for parasailing, beach shacks, golden sands, and lively markets.
description: Known as the Queen of Beaches, Calangute spans a long sandy stretch lined with sunbeds, lively beach shacks offering Goan cuisine, water sports centers, and vibrant shopping streets.
history: Transformed in the 1960s and 70s into an international coastal destination.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Baga Beach
summary: Lively North Goa beach famous for Tito Lane nightlife, dolphin cruises, water sports, and Baga Creek.
description: Baga Beach sits adjacent to Calangute along the Baga Creek estuary, famous for thrilling water sports, sunset beach dining, and legendary music clubs including Tito and Cafe Mambo.
history: A traditional fishing village that blossomed into a world-famous coastal party and entertainment hub.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Anjuna Beach
summary: Bohemian North Goa beach renowned for red laterite rock formations, Wednesday flea market, and sunset trance parties.
description: Anjuna Beach is world-famous for its free-spirited culture, scenic rocky cliffs, Curlies beach shack, and the bustling weekly Wednesday Flea Market selling handicrafts, jewelry, and eclectic art.
history: Epicenter of 1960s hippie trail and birthplace of Goa Trance electronic music culture.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Palolem Beach
summary: Scenic white-sand crescent bay in South Goa lined with leaning coconut palms, calm turquoise waters, and dolphin cruises.
description: Palolem is celebrated for its natural semi-circular crescent bay framed by wooded headlands. Its gentle, shallow waters make it one of the safest beaches for swimming, sea-kayaking to Butterfly Beach, and silent headphone parties.
history: A tranquil Konkan fishing village that emerged into an international sanctuary for wellness, yoga, and sustainable coastal tourism.
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa

name: Fontainhas
summary: UNESCO-recognized heritage Latin Quarter in Panaji known for colorful 18th-century Portuguese houses, narrow lanes, and azulejos tiles.
description: Fontainhas is Goa historic Latin Quarter, built at the base of Altinho hill. Featuring vibrant terracotta-roofed Portuguese homes painted in yellow, blue, and green, charming wrought-iron balconies, cozy bakeries, and art galleries.
history: Developed in the late 18th century by Antonio Joao de Sequeira; declared a heritage conservation zone in 1984.
visiting_hours: Open 24 Hours (Best for walking: 08:00 AM - 11:00 AM & 04:00 PM - 07:00 PM)
source_name: Department of Tourism, Government of Goa
